chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"The single Takbirah at the opening of the prayer is sufficient, and the three are better, and the seven are better than all of them."

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior/better (indicating recommended virtue over mere sufficiency).
key_terms.افْتِتَاحِ الصَّلَاةِ: The opening of the prayer, specifically the initial standing and declaration.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَةُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' or a related glorification; here referring to the specific dhikr recited at the start of prayer.
key_terms.كُلِّهِ: All of them (referring to the total set of options mentioned: one, three, or seven).

ai.seo_question: How many glorifications should be recited during the opening Takbir of the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of excellence in the opening glorifications (Tasbihat) of the prayer, distinguishing between legal sufficiency and spiritual merit. It establishes that while a single glorification fulfills the basic obligation, reciting three is superior, and seven is the most virtuous, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Fadl* (supererogatory excellence) within the structure of *Wajib* (obligatory) acts. This ruling underscores the principle that while the minimum requirement ensures validity, increasing devotion enhances the quality of worship.
